articles.title: How the 3M Stock Turnaround Is Happening Faster Than Expected
articles.summary: 3M Company is turning around quickly after years of litigation-related concerns.
articles.body:
Industrial conglomerate 3M (MMM) is undergoing a swift turnaround on Wall Street, driven by stronger execution and margin expansion. The company has been under fire for years due to heavy litigation pressure. It has paid more than $10 billion in settlements to resolve claims of polluting water bodies with PFAs, or "forever chemicals." 3M has also begun settling a $6 billion payment to veterans over earplugs that caused hearing loss.

However, the company seems to be moving past that phase, as investors focus on potential growth and margin expansion. 3M CEO William Brown said the company's on-time, in-full (OTIF) deliveries have improved from the low 80% range to about 90%, with some consumer-business units consistently achieving rates in the mid-90% range.

This has also been complemented by a flurry of product launches. Brown said 3M has planned more than 350 launches this year. New products are expected to account for 20% of sales by the end of 2027. Citing expanded beam optical technology as a promising data center opportunity, Brown said 3M expects to generate roughly $400 million in growth above its underlying markets this year. This faster-than-expected turnaround has been highly effective.

3M is a diversified manufacturing and technology company headquartered in St. Paul, Minnesota. It makes products for industries such as healthcare, transportation, electronics, construction, and consumer goods. Its products include safety equipment, medical supplies, adhesives, filters, automotive materials, packaging products, and cleaning items. The company has a market capitalization of $83.88 billion.

3M sells its products worldwide through direct sales, distributors, retailers, and online channels. The company uses its expertise in science, engineering, and manufacturing to develop practical solutions for businesses and consumers. Its operations cover research, product development, manufacturing, and global distribution across several major industries.

Over the past 52 weeks, 3M's stock has gained 3.9%, while it has gained 1.6% year-to-date. This suggests investors view the stock as a turnaround and income name, not a fast-growing company. 3M's stock reached a 52-week high of $184.90 on July 28, but is down 12% from that level. Currently, 3M is trading cheaper than its peers. Its forward-adjusted price-to-earnings (non-GAAP) ratio of 18.18x is lower than the industry average of 19.17x.

articles.title: The 11 S&P 500 Sectors Are Fading Quickly. Protect Yourself Against a Stock Market Crash Now.

articles.body:
Headline stock indexes can easily mask underlying market weakness, and that's exactly what I think is happening right now.

When I look under the hood at sector-level momentum, I see risk increasing. This is not a new development. But if the trend is our friend, it's telling us that "winter's coming."

Check out this snapshot as of Wednesday's market close of ROAR Scores – my proprietary technical analysis system – for all 11 S&P 500 Index ($SPX) sectors. ROAR is designed to identify the risks associated with investing in any ETF or stock.

I then built my "ROAR Score" into a full-fledged DIY security analysis, portfolio construction, and investment research platform, with the help of my friends at PiTrade.com.

Using this toolset, I can take a close look at the 11 sectors, where I see a budding breakdown. That is a strong hint to me that market breadth is quietly deteriorating, with sector after sector rolling over into technical weakness.

Understanding the ROAR Score and How to Use It to Manage Risk

The ROAR Score is a quantitative risk-management metric engineered to evaluate "Return Opportunity And Risk (ROAR)." I do not mean risk of a minor pullback. We all know how much short-term noise exists in this algorithmically driven, S&P 500 Index fund-obsessed market. I'm talking about the risk of "major" loss.

Depending on how volatile a stock or ETF typically is, that could be a 10%-20% move in most cases. One simple way to think of ROAR is that it seeks to answer the question "what are the odds that the next 10% move is UP and not DOWN?" The score can be loosely interpreted that way.

However, as I emphasize regularly to subscribers, the TREND in the score is more important than the actual "spot" score today.

The most powerful use of ROAR analysis is to combine securities and use the platform to automate the allocation among that set of tickers and backtest before investing. That essentially creates a programmatic approach to buying, selling, and position-sizing.

Yes, there are many systems that sound like that. But as my regular readers here know, I'm not the "how do I double my money in a year?" guy. I'm a RISK MANAGEMENT pro. Everything else is secondary. So ROAR is more like a 21st century version of combining securities with the goal of not losing big along the way. To me, that's the way to create successful long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Dear Tesla Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for September 30
articles.summary: Tesla’s Cybercab-related deadline could provide investors with a key update on the regulatory path for its ambitious Robotaxi strategy.
articles.body:
Tesla (TSLA) investors have a key date to watch as the company's ambitious Robotaxi strategy faces a fresh regulatory test. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has requested Tesla to answer a series of questions by Sept. 30 regarding how the company self-certified its Cybercab as compliant with federal motor vehicle safety standards. The inquiry comes shortly after Tesla began commercial deployment of Cybercab in Austin, Texas on Sept. 3.

The NHTSA is examining the technical data and certification process Tesla relied on, including whether temporarily installed human-driver controls or other equipment played a role in establishing compliance. The agency is also asking whether the Cybercab can be driven by a human, whether occupants can move the vehicle through touchscreen controls, and what limits apply to its speed, operating hours, and more. The questions are particularly significant because the Cybercab lacks conventional controls such as a steering wheel, accelerator and brake pedals, as well as a rearview mirror.

With robotaxis emerging as an increasingly important part of Tesla's long-term growth strategy, the company's Sept. 30 response could provide investors with greater clarity on the regulatory path for scaling Cybercab in the United States.

Tesla is an automotive and clean energy company headquartered in Austin, Texas. Tesla designs, manufactures, and sells electric vehicles (EVs) alongside energy storage solutions such as Powerwall and Megapack, solar products, and related services. Over the years, Tesla has expanded globally with a network of production facilities, showrooms, service centers, and Supercharger stations. The company has also increasingly emphasized advanced software and autonomous capabilities as part of its long-term strategy. Tesla is one of the world's most valuable companies with a current market capitalization of $1.4 trillion.

TSLA stock has struggled to keep pace with the company's steady push into EVs, autonomous driving, robotics, and artificial intelligence (AI) this year. The stock closed at $364.27 on Sept. 18, down slightly after a recent rebound. Shares have gained about 8% over the past month, but the broader picture remains challenging; TSLA stock is still down 19% year-to-date (YTD) and about 27% below its 52-week high of $498.83. The stock has slumped 13% over the past year.

articles.title: Nebius’s Price Hike Suggests Michael Burry Made a Mistake and Is Shorting the Best Neocloud Stock
articles.summary: After closing his short position against CoreWeave, the question is whether Burry is still bearish on Nebius, or just waiting for a better exit point.
articles.body:
On August 7, Michael Burry revealed a new short position in Nebius Group (NBIS). Rather than paying what he described as exorbitant prices for puts, Burry chose to short the equity directly. The move represents a particularly clear bearish call on a rapidly growing AI infrastructure company. Michael Burry's timing is particularly notable because Nvidia (NVDA) recently disclosed a 9.3% stake in Nebius. Moreover, multiple comparisons have also favored NBIS over CoreWeave (CRWV) as the stronger of the two major neocloud companies. In fact, I also pointed this out in my Nebius vs. CoreWeave article a while back. Burry's trade raises a key question: Does he believe Nebius is nearing the peak valuation, or is the market simply overestimating a company that many investors see as one of the sector's strongest players?

Burry Bets Against Nebius While Returning To Oracle

Burry's recently disclosed short position in Nebius at $211.77 per share reflects his broader concerns about growing leverage risk from off-balance-sheet commitments across the technology and cloud sectors. He also reopened a short in Oracle (ORCL) at $144.63 per share, just days after closing his previous position in the stock for a substantial profit. That earlier trade involved January 2027 puts with strikes in the low 100s, although Burry said he could return to puts if volatility falls. And just a few days ago, Burry closed his short position in CoreWeave. As he is still short Nebius, it makes me wonder whether he is really bearish on the company, or just waiting for a better exit point. However, last Thursday, Nebius announced it was raising compute prices for selected Nvidia chips starting Oct. 1 — another piece of bad news for Burry.

Why Nebius May Be the Wrong Neocloud to Bet Against?

The case against a Nebius short starts with Nvidia's investment. The shares surged more than 18% in a single session after Nvidia disclosed its stake in Nebius. The investment signals strong support from one of the AI industry's most important suppliers. Nebius had $9.37 billion in cash against $9.48 billion in debt. By comparison, CoreWeave held $2.27 billion in cash against $35.15 billion in debt. This highlights Nebius' significantly stronger balance sheet relative to CoreWeave.

articles.title: Domino's Pizza Stock Is Dirt Cheap, With 30% Potential Upside - What's the Best Play?

articles.body:
Domino's Pizza (DPZ) stock keeps falling. DPZ is at least 30% too cheap, based on its strong free cash flow (FCF) and high FCF margins. Two attractive plays are to sell short out-of-the-money (OTM) put options with near-term expiration dates, as well as buy long-dated in-the-money (ITM) calls.

DPZ dropped to $294.20 on Friday, Sept. 18, near its 6-month low price of $283.03 on June 23. This was about a month before its July 23 Q2 earnings release.

After that, DPZ floated higher. Maybe that same pattern will return, as Q3 earnings are due out on Oct. 13.

Moreover, the stock is well below both analysts' price targets. In addition, DPZ is well below historical forward price/earnings (P/E) metrics. More on that below.

However, one reason why it is weak may be that analysts have slightly lowered their revenue projections. For example, 2026 revenue forecasts are now $5.18 billion , down from $5.2 billion as reported in my July 21 Barchart article (" Domino's Pizza Delivers Strong FCF and FCF Margins - Is DPZ Stock Too Cheap? ")

In addition, analysts are forecasting $5.30 billion for 2027, down from $5.37 billion in prior average forecast surveys. Some are concerned Domino's faces weak demand, increasing competition, and is closing stores faster than expected.

Nevertheless, its FCF is still strong. Last quarter it generated a 14% FCF margin, and its trailing 12-month (TTM) margin was 13% of sales.

That implies that over the next 12 months (NTM), its average $5.24 billion in sales could generate 4681 million in FCF.

So, using a 5% FCF yield metric, its market value should be $13.6 billion ($5.24b/0.05), compared to its existing $9.733 billion market cap. That implies a price target (PT) 40% higher, or $411.88 per share.

Other analysts also see significantly higher PTs: $381.11 (Yahoo! Finance), $383.21 (Barchart), and $411.93 (AnaChart).

Moreover, a third valuation metric is its forward P/E ratio. Over the last 5 years, DPZ has had an average forward P/E of 24.46x according to Morningstar, and 26.76x (Seeking Alpha).

So, using a rough average multiple of 25x and applying analysts' 2026 EPS forecast of $19.04, DPZ's value is $476 per share. Even at a 25% discount to the average forward P/E, the PT is $357.00 , or 21% higher.

articles.title: Ask These 2 Questions to Make Sure Your Roth Conversion Doesn't End Up Backfiring
articles.summary: If you're going to do a conversion, you want it to make sense.
articles.body:
There's a reason Roth conversions are often touted as a smart retirement strategy.

A Roth conversion allows you to move funds from a traditional IRA or 401(k) plan to a Roth IRA. From there, you get to enjoy all of the benefits that come with a Roth. That means your money gets to grow tax-free, you can take tax-free withdrawals, and you won't be subjected to required minimum distributions (RMDs).

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

But that doesn't mean a Roth conversion is a smart choice for you. So before you move forward with one, make sure to ask yourself these key questions.

A Roth conversion is a taxable event. If you do a $200,000 Roth conversion, for example, you'll owe taxes on that $200,000 the year you move it over. So the key is to make sure the taxes you'll pay on a conversion are lower than the taxes you'll pay on withdrawals. If that's not the case, the conversion may not pay off.

For example, let's say you plan to work up until your RMD age and earn $100,000 a year during that time. Based on your job-related paycheck, Social Security benefits, and conversion amount, you may be looking at converting funds at a 32% federal tax rate.

But if you expect your federal tax bracket in retirement to be 22% because your paycheck from work will be gone at that point, then it doesn't make sense to pay a higher rate of tax on a conversion. In that case, you're giving the government more money.

2. Do I want to be charitable in retirement?

Another thing to consider before a Roth conversion is how charitable you want to be. QCDs, or qualified charitable distributions, allow you to send funds from an IRA to a registered charity directly. Going this route bypasses taxes but also satisfies your RMDs.

If you're going to donate a significant chunk of your savings to charity, it may not make sense to do a Roth conversion. With a conversion, you're paying taxes to move your money into a Roth when you'd potentially be avoiding taxes on that money anyway.

A Roth conversion could be a smart way to minimize taxes in retirement and gain more control over your savings by getting out of RMDs. But before you move forward, confirm that the math actually makes sense. Otherwise, you may end up regretting your decision to do a conversion after the fact.

articles.title: Inside Ciena’s 2029 Roadmap: Ambitious Targets Meet Bullish Analyst Ratings
articles.summary: Ciena has unveiled its ambitious 2029 targets aiming for 30% CAGR growth through 2029.
articles.body:
Ciena (CIEN) is a technology company specializing in optical transport systems, routing and switching platforms, and automation software for high-speed connectivity. Founded in 1992, the company serves telecommunications carriers, cloud and data-center operators, cable providers, and enterprise customers worldwide. The company has emerged as a critical enabler of the AI infrastructure boom, with its leading multiplexers, switches, and coherent optical routers connecting GPU clusters across hyperscale data centers. Under CEO Gary Smith, Ciena continues capitalizing on surging bandwidth demand tied to cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and data-center interconnect buildouts across global networks.

Ciena's stock performance in 2026 has been nothing short of a rollercoaster. Shares recently traded around $334, up more than 43% year-to-date and a striking 152% over the past 12 months. Yet it is still sitting roughly 48% below the 52-week and all-time high of $637.51 reached back in June. Remarkably, the stock has tumbled sharply even after posting back-to-back earnings beats, as sky-high investor expectations set the bar so high that the market rewarded strong results with selloffs.

For context, the S&P 500 Information Technology index ($SRIT) has gained roughly 22% year-to-date, itself an impressive run during the AI boom. Ciena has significantly outpaced that broader benchmark on a trailing basis, even though its recent sharp swings underscore just how much more volatile this stock is compared to the sector at large.

Record-Setting Fiscal Third-Quarter Results

Ciena's fiscal third-quarter 2026 results were genuinely historic. Revenue hit a record $1.67 billion, up 37% year-over-year and ahead of the $1.64 billion analyst consensus. Adjusted earnings skyrocketed 215% to $2.11 per share, beating estimates by more than 22% — one of the strongest quarters in company history, fueled by surging AI-related network investment and optical interconnect demand.

articles.title: Is Atlassian Stock Still a Buy After a 132% Three-Month Run? Here’s What Analysts Are Saying.
articles.summary: Key TakeawaysAtlassian stock has climbed 132% since mid-June, moving from roughly $83 to $192. 02 by September 18, after a run of AI-driven software earnings...
articles.body:
Atlassian stock has climbed 132% since mid-June, moving from roughly $83 to $192.02 by September 18, after a run of AI-driven software earnings beats flipped the sector's disruption narrative into a tailwind story.

Wall Street carries 21 buy ratings, 6 outperforms and 6 holds on Atlassian stock.

TIKR's mid case model still sees Atlassian stock reaching $279 by June 2031, a 45% total return that works out to 8% annualized.

The Street's mean target has only crept from $140 in June to $199 now, and the target-to-price ratio has collapsed from 180% to 104% as the stock did the analysts' work for them.

Why Atlassian Stock Has Soared 132% in Three Months on an AI Rerating

Atlassian (TEAM) stock has climbed 132% over the past three months, according to TIKR's own chart data, rising from roughly $83 in mid-June to $192.02 at the September 18 close. The move did not come from a single announcement. It came from three separate earnings prints, each one chipping away at a bear case that had cut Atlassian stock nearly in half earlier in 2026.

That bear case had a clear origin point. On July 14, IBM warned that customer spending was shifting away from software toward chips, servers and storage far faster than expected, and the stock fell 25% in a single session. Atlassian, ServiceNow and Adobe all sold off on the read-through, feeding a narrative that AI coding tools would let enterprises build their own replacements for platforms like Jira.

Atlassian answered that narrative directly on August 6, when fiscal fourth-quarter revenue rose 28% year over year to $1.77 billion, cloud revenue grew 31%, and remaining performance obligations jumped 44% to $4.82 billion. Shares that had closed at $113.32 the day before soared more than 28% in extended trading. Then Salesforce beat on August 19 and rolled out a Claude integration, sending its own stock up as much as 21.6% and lifting Atlassian alongside ServiceNow and Adobe. Snowflake followed on September 3 with a raised revenue forecast, and its 25% pop buoyed Atlassian, Salesforce and Adobe again.

CFO James Chuong made the case explicit at the Citi Global TMT Conference on September 9: "AI is going to be a tailwind for Atlassian as customers look to really drive more and more value out of AI, understanding that Atlassian delivers an incredible graph, our Teamwork Graph, that's what's really going to be powering AI across the enterprise." Three peer confirmations in five weeks turned that claim from a talking point into a pattern investors were willing to pay for.

articles.title: Delta's Non-Main-Cabin Revenue Hits 61% in 2026 -- Why It Matters for Earnings
articles.summary: The leading network airline is a very different business from what it was a decade ago, and it might be time for the market to rerate its stock.
articles.body:
The airline industry is notorious for its cyclicality. Traditionally, airlines like Delta Air Lines (NYSE: DAL) are seen as having strong pricing power when travel demand is high, only to suffer when demand wanes, as ticket prices decline while the airline continues to carry high fixed costs.

That said, Delta might not be as risky as you think, and the market may need to rethink how it values the company. Here's why.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Delta Air Lines is diversifying its revenue streams

Chief Commercial Officer Joe Esposito outlined on the second-quarter earnings call that "diverse revenue streams represented 61% of total revenue in the quarter, up 2 points over last year, with premium and loyalty revenue both up nearly 20%."

The 61% figure is impressive enough, and it makes sense to create an apples-to-apples comparison across the industry, as other airlines don't operate refineries (which is a low-margin business anyway). Still, I would argue that it underplays the issue.

By "diverse revenue streams," Esposito means Delta's non-main-cabin revenue. That's fair enough, but when calculating the 61%, Delta adjusts the revenue figure by stripping out its refinery sales to third parties. Esposito is referring to the bottom figure on the right side of the table, but including refinery sales increases the share of non-main-cabin revenue to 65.3%.

Data source: Delta Air Lines presentations. * Adjusted figure excludes $2.091 billion in third-party refinery sales.

Sticking with my figure of 65.3%, it represents a significant increase over the full-year 2017 equivalent figure of 50%. Back then, main cabin revenue was 1.7 times Delta's premium cabin revenue, but as you can see above, Delta's premium cabin revenue exceeded main cabin revenue in the second quarter.

It's all part of a deliberate strategy to diversify Delta's revenue away from the extreme cyclicality of main cabin ticket revenue. As Esposito noted on the recent earnings call: "We're not growing Main Cabin seats. This is a multiyear, several years in a row, that we haven't grown this cabin. We won't be growing it next year either."

articles.title: Gold Has Gone Sideways, But These 3 Stocks Haven’t
articles.summary: While gold trades roughly flat YTD, Coeur Mining, Alamos Gold, and Wheaton Precious Metals have outperformed, boosted by strong earnings, free cash flow, and...
articles.body:
Gold is trading roughly flat year to date in 2026, while gold miners and metals streaming companies have outperformed the metal itself.

Coeur Mining, Alamos Gold, and Wheaton Precious Metals have each posted recent share price gains, supported by strong free cash flow, dividends, and buybacks.

Each company faces distinct challenges, including reduced guidance from Coeur and Alamos and Wheaton's dependence on gold and silver spot prices.

The price of gold briefly dipped surrounding the Federal Reserve's recent announcement of its first interest rate hike in three years, but quickly rebounded. After the incredible multi-quarter rally in recent years, gold has had a more tumultuous 2026 so far, but is essentially trading flat year to date (YTD). The same is not true, however, for a number of companies involved in the gold production industry—both miners and metals streaming firms—all of which have outperformed the precious metal itself over the same period.

While a confluence of factors is likely to impact the price of gold through the end of the year, from central bank buying trends and evolving geopolitics to ongoing inflation, higher interest rates, and changing U.S. dollar strength, investors may feel that a position in one or more of these companies is more stable than buying up more bullion or gold futures.

Coeur's Transformation Is Ongoing and Significant

Coeur Mining (NYSE: CDE) drew investor attention earlier in the year for its strong performance and share price under $20; it is now trading just above that threshold, but despite not being quite as cheap, its impressive growth may very well still warrant consideration. Coeur's latest earnings report in August was promising in multiple ways. Despite a moderate revenue miss and a more significant earnings per share (EPS) miss, Coeur still reported record quarterly performance with $1.1 billion in revenue, adjusted EBITDA at a sizable $478 million, and healthy free cash flow.

The company's major acquisitions and expansions are underway and should contribute to H2 2026 performance, even as inflation has threatened to undercut profits. What may have scared investors is that Coeur's guidance was cut due to these operational headwinds, but fundamentally, the company still offers many compelling attributes as a business. In the meantime, its growing pile of cash has made it possible to launch a new dividend and share buyback program. Looking at Coeur's situation from just a couple of years ago, when it faced major debt challenges, and comparing it to today—with free cash flow sufficient to return value to shareholders—it may be clearer why CDE shares are up about 7% in the last month.

articles.title: ‘Even Though It’s Bad for Berkshire’ Billionaire Charlie Munger Said to Skip Insurance Because ‘You’re Paying for the Other Fellow’s Frauds’
articles.summary: The advice came with a condition: insure anything you could not comfortably afford to replace out of your own pocket.
articles.body:
The late Charlie Munger spent most of his life as vice chairman of Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.A) (BRK.B) a company built on insurance. In February 2023, at the annual meeting of Daily Journal Corporation (DJCO), where he was chairman, he was asked about self-insurance and answered in a way that worked against his own company's interests. "With one exception, I've never carried collision insurance on a car, and once I got rich, I stopped carrying fire insurance on houses," he said. "I just self-insure. That is the right way to do it."

Becky Quick, moderating, put the obvious point to him: he was the number two at a group stuffed with insurers; why not just tell people to insure everything? "I'd rather tell it the way it is than tell it in a way that helps Berkshire. I'm not going to tell it differently than I think it really is just because it's better for Berkshire. Even though it's bad for Berkshire, I will tell you that if you can afford to self-insure, then self-insure," Munger said.

He continued, "You should insure against things that you can't afford to pay for yourself." He continued, "But if you can afford to take the bumps, some unusual expense coming along doesn't really hurt you that much, why would you want to fool around with some insurance company if your house burned down?" He was describing people who could write a check for a replacement house. For anyone who could not, his own rule points the other way.

This ideology has limitations, however: almost every mortgage lender requires homeowners coverage, and virtually every auto lender requires collision on a financed car, so the choice Munger described is unavailable to most people who have not already paid off the asset. Liability coverage is separate again because the exposure is open-ended rather than capped at the value of the thing insured, and it is not a candidate for self-insurance in a normal household. Further, many states around the U.S. require liability insurance to drive a vehicle on the road.

articles.title: Funcionários da Caixa rejeitam proposta e greve continua; como ficam as contas e benefícios? | G1
articles.standfirst: Em assembleia nesta segunda (21), 59,3% dos empregados votaram contra a proposta; principal impasse nas negociações é o Saúde Caixa, plano de saúde dos trabalhadores.
articles.summary: Em assembleia nesta segunda (21), 59,3% dos empregados votaram contra a proposta; principal impasse nas negociações é o Saúde Caixa, plano de saúde dos trabalhadores.
articles.body:
Os empregados da Caixa Econômica Federal rejeitaram nesta segunda-feira (21) a última proposta do banco para o Acordo Coletivo de Trabalho. Em assembleia virtual realizada pelo Sindicato dos Bancários de São Paulo, Osasco e Região, 59,3% dos participantes votaram contra a oferta.

A votação ocorreu entre 11h e 18h. Após o resultado, o comando de greve se reuniu para discutir os próximos passos. A paralisação continua nesta terça-feira (22).

O principal impasse nas negociações é o Saúde Caixa , plano de saúde dos empregados, segundo os representantes dos trabalhadores.

Com a volta da paralisação, como ficam as contas e os pagamentos dos benefícios sociais, como o Bolsa Família?

Consumidor deve continuar pagando normalmente

Segundo o Procon-SP, a greve não afasta a obrigação de pagar as contas dentro do prazo de vencimento. Por isso, o consumidor deve ficar atento às datas para evitar a cobrança de juros.

O órgão orienta que os pagamentos sejam feitos, quando disponíveis, pelos sites ou aplicativos dos bancos. Também é possível recorrer a redes de supermercados e casas lotéricas que recebem boletos e contas de água, luz, gás e telefone.

E se não conseguir pagar por causa da greve?

Fernando Canutto, sócio do Godke Advogados e especialista em direito bancário, explica que, quando a instituição mantém atendimento presencial, o Banco Central estabelece que ela não pode simplesmente impedir, recusar ou dificultar o atendimento sob o argumento de que existem canais eletrônicos.

Segundo ele, o banco deve procurar garantir meios razoáveis para a continuidade dos serviços essenciais.

O advogado ressalta, porém, que existe uma diferença entre a agência estar fechada e o consumidor estar efetivamente impossibilitado de realizar a operação. Com a digitalização dos serviços bancários, essa distinção ganhou importância.

Por outro lado, se o cliente conseguir demonstrar que tentou pagar dentro do prazo e que isso se tornou impossível por uma circunstância relacionada à indisponibilidade do serviço bancário, poderá contestar multa, juros e outros efeitos da mora.

Sim . Segundo o Procon-SP, depósitos e saques podem ser realizados em caixas eletrônicos.

O órgão, porém, recomenda que, na ausência de funcionários da instituição bancária, o consumidor evite a ajuda de terceiros ao utilizar os terminais. Isso porque a guarda da senha e do cartão é de responsabilidade do correntista.

Como ficam os pagamentos do Bolsa Família? Também são interrompidos?

Mesmo com a greve dos bancários, os pagamentos do Bolsa Família serão realizados normalmente, segundo o banco.

A Caixa informou que os canais de pagamento dos benefícios sociais permanecem funcionando e que os beneficiários poderão acessar os recursos sem precisar comparecer às agências.

O banco ainda explicou que os pagamentos serão, em sua maioria, por meio de crédito em contas bancárias. O dinheiro pode ser movimentado pelos aplicativos Caixa TEM e App Caixa ou pelo cartão de débito vinculado à conta.

Os recursos podem ser usados para fazer PIX, pagar contas e boletos e realizar compras em estabelecimentos comerciais. Também é possível sacar o dinheiro nos canais disponíveis.

Os funcionários da Caixa estão em greve nacional desde 10 de setembro , após rejeitarem a proposta anterior de renovação do Acordo Coletivo de Trabalho. Nesta segunda, os trabalhadores rejeitaram a segunda proposta do banco.

A paralisação começou após mais de 90% das bases sindicais rejeitarem a oferta apresentada pelo banco , de acordo com a Contraf-CUT. O Saúde Caixa era apontado pelas entidades como um dos principais pontos de discordância nas negociações.

Enquanto os empregados da Caixa decidiram entrar em greve por tempo indeterminado, a categoria bancária já havia assinado a Convenção Coletiva de Trabalho com a Federação Nacional dos Bancos (Fenaban).

articles.title: Entenda por que Minas acompanha resultado das eleições presidenciais desde 1989 | G1
articles.standfirst: Reportagens mostram semelhanças econômicas, sociais e eleitorais entre o estado e o país e os desafios para quem assumir o governo de Minas em 2027.
articles.summary: Reportagens mostram semelhanças econômicas, sociais e eleitorais entre o estado e o país e os desafios para quem assumir o governo de Minas em 2027.
articles.body:
Imagem aérea de Belo Horizonte — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Desde a primeira eleição direta para presidente após a ditadura militar, em 1989, o candidato que venceu a disputa em Minas Gerais também foi eleito presidente da República. Em diferentes pleitos, os percentuais registrados no estado ficaram próximos dos resultados nacionais.

A diversidade social, econômica e regional de Minas ajuda a explicar as semelhanças com o restante do país. O estado reúne características de diferentes regiões brasileiras, que aparecem na formação da população, na economia e também no comportamento dos eleitores.

Essas semelhanças são tema do primeiro episódio de uma nova série de reportagens da TV Globo, exibida a partir desta segunda-feira (21) no MG2. A série mostra diferentes realidades de Minas Gerais e os desafios para quem assumir o governo do estado a partir de 2027.

Minas faz divisa com seis estados e o Distrito Federal. Segundo Bruno Durão, professor do Departamento de Geografia da PUC Minas, a localização e o processo histórico de ocupação ajudam a explicar as diferenças entre as regiões do estado.

O Norte e o Nordeste mineiros receberam influência de populações vindas do Nordeste do país. A região Central foi marcada pelo ciclo do ouro, enquanto Sul, Sudeste e Zona da Mata tiveram influência de movimentos de ocupação e atividades econômicas de São Paulo e do Rio de Janeiro.

As diferenças também aparecem na economia. As regiões Metropolitana, Central, Oeste e Zona da Mata concentram 52,89% do PIB mineiro, percentual próximo à participação do Sudeste no PIB brasileiro, de 53,13%.

O Sul de Minas e o Campo das Vertentes representam 16,10% da economia estadual, enquanto a Região Sul responde por 16,81% do PIB nacional. Norte de Minas e Jequitinhonha concentram 5,49% do PIB estadual.

Desde a primeira eleição direta para presidente após a ditadura militar, em 1989, Minas acompanha o resultado nacional.

Em 1989, candidatos de direita venceram no estado e no país. Em 1994 e 1998, foram candidatos mais ao centro. Depois, candidatos de esquerda venceram quatro eleições consecutivas, entre 2002 e 2014. Em 2018, candidatos de direita voltaram a vencer. Em 2022, a esquerda recebeu novamente a maioria dos votos.

Na última eleição presidencial, os percentuais de Minas ficaram próximos dos nacionais. No segundo turno de 2022, o candidato de esquerda recebeu 50,21% dos votos válidos no estado e 50,90% no Brasil. O candidato de direita teve 49,79% em Minas e 49,10% no país.

O cientista político Felipe Nunes, professor da FGV e diretor da Quaest, define Minas como um “estado pêndulo”.

“É um eleitorado que está disposto a mudar de opinião e de posição”, afirma.

O comportamento dos eleitores também varia dentro do estado.

Em 2022, Norte de Minas e Jequitinhonha deram maioria dos votos à esquerda, assim como ocorreu no Nordeste brasileiro. No Sul de Minas e Campo das Vertentes e no Triângulo, Alto Paranaíba e Noroeste, a direita teve maioria, comportamento semelhante ao registrado nas regiões Sul e Centro-Oeste do país.

Nas regiões Metropolitana, Central, Oeste e Zona da Mata, a direita também ficou à frente, assim como ocorreu no Sudeste brasileiro. Nos vales do Rio Doce e Mucuri, o resultado ficou mais equilibrado, a exemplo da Região Norte do país.

Para Lucas Gelape, professor de Ciência Política da UFMG, o tamanho do eleitorado e a diversidade regional ajudam a explicar a importância de Minas nas eleições.

Segundo ele, o estado é econômica e politicamente desconcentrado, o que exige dos candidatos atenção às diferentes regiões, e não apenas a Belo Horizonte .

articles.title: Governo encontra espaço fiscal de R$ 19,6 bilhões no orçamento; parte vai bancar reajuste do Bolsa Família, diz ministro   | G1
articles.standfirst: Em entrevista ao g1, o ministro do Planejamento, Bruno Moretti negou que a medida tenha sido tomada com foco nas eleições.
articles.summary: Em entrevista ao g1, o ministro do Planejamento, Bruno Moretti negou que a medida tenha sido tomada com foco nas eleições.
articles.body:
Bruno Moretti, ministro do Planejamento e Orçamento — Foto: Edilson Rodrigues/Agência Senado

O ministro do Planejamento, Bruno Moretti, afirmou em entrevista ao g1 que o governo identificou um espaço fiscal de R$ 19,6 bilhões no orçamento deste ano e, por isso, decidiu reajustar o Bolsa Família .

"Você tem uma queda [de despesas] projetada nessa ordem de grandeza. O Bolsa Família já será incorporado, portanto, às nossas regras fiscais. A gente fez realmente uma medida para a qual a gente tinha espaço fiscal, portanto, sem qualquer tipo de burla, absoluto respeito às convenções e às regras fiscais", disse o ministro.

Segundo o ministro, a folga orçamentária estimada neste momento veio da redução da projeção de gastos com a Previdência Social, o Benefício de Prestação Continuada (BPC), pessoal e subsídios.

O detalhamento será divulgado pelo governo no Relatório de Avaliação de Receitas e Despesas até quinta-feira (24).

O reajuste do Bolsa Família terá impacto de R$ 5,8 bilhões em 2026. No ano que vem, o custo será de R$ 22,7 bilhões.

O ministro disse que, nesse caso, enviará mensagem modificativa com a previsão, sem, contudo, alterar os compromissos fiscais já assumidos para o ano que vem.

"Zero. Nenhum efeito em regras fiscais".

Com a correção de cerca de 15%, o piso do programa passará de R$ 600 para R$ 691. O novo valor começará a ser pago em 19 de outubro, entre o primeiro e o segundo turnos (se houver) das eleições presidenciais.

Desde que foi relançado pelo governo Lula, em março de 2023, o Bolsa Família não era reajustado. Moretti negou que a medida tenha sido tomada com foco nas eleições.

"Se tivesse uma medida de caráter eleitoreiro, populista, o que aconteceria é que ela seria tomada no improviso e, na verdade, nós só autorizamos, só demos o ateste orçamentário, a partir do momento em que a gente verificou que havia o espaço fiscal".

Depois do anúncio, economistas alertaram para possíveis impactos sobre as contas públicas.

"A proximidade com o cenário eleitoral foi casuística. Na verdade, o que importou aqui foi o recebimento das informações finais do relatório, nos dando a segurança de que havia o espaço fiscal."

Na sexta-feira (18), o ministro Gilmar Mendes, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), decidiu que o decreto que reajusta o valor do benefício do Bolsa Família não fere as regras eleitorais . O ministro afirmou que o aumento concedido apenas atualiza os valores pelo critério de correção monetária.

Veja os principais pontos da entrevista:

g1: Por que o reajuste de 15,04% no Bolsa Família só ocorreu agora? Bruno Moretti: O que a gente apurou, e nós vamos publicar no próximo relatório bimestral de avaliação de receitas e despesas, na semana que vem, é que as despesas que estavam bloqueadas para custear os benefícios previdenciários, os benefícios pagos pelo INSS, tiveram as projeções relativas a essas despesas revistas, e elas se reduziram um pouco. Posso até te dizer a ordem de grandeza: só considerando os benefícios previdenciários, uma redução da projeção de crescimento em R$ 11,5 bilhões. Significa que esse recurso havia sido reservado para essa finalidade e fica disponibilizado para outras finalidades. Portanto, abriu-se o espaço fiscal. Basicamente, é uma despesa que ocorreria com benefícios do INSS. Parcela da redução dessa projeção eu canalizo para o Bolsa Família. Então, fazer com responsabilidade significa fazer desde que haja o espaço fiscal correspondente. E editamos o decreto [com o reajuste do Bolsa Família].

g1: Além da rubrica da Previdência, quais outras observaram a mesma tendência de queda? Bruno Moretti: Para 2026, nós vamos dar transparência a isso no relatório do dia 24 [de setembro], mas eu posso te adiantar que o valor da Previdência é duas vezes maior do que o reajuste do Bolsa Família. Tem alguma queda projetada para o Benefício de Prestação Continuada (BPC) também, tem alguma queda projetada para despesa de pessoal, tem alguma queda projetada em subsídios, de maneira que elas significam mais ou menos R$ 19,6 bilhões de redução projetada para a despesa obrigatória.

g1: E para 2027? Bruno Moretti: Para 2027, como eu te disse, a gente ainda está fechando as contas, porque a mensagem [modificativa, alterando o projeto de orçamento 2027] vem depois do relatório. Está concentrado no relatório e depois vai afinar as contas. Mas, fundamentalmente, a gente vai demonstrar que o espaço reside nessas mesmas rubricas: despesa previdenciária, um pouco de pessoal, um pouco em BPC, fruto dessa projeção reduzida agora de 2026, que rebate lá em 2027.

g1: Não vai mudar a projeção de superávit? Bruno Moretti: Zero. Nenhum efeito em regras fiscais.

g1: Os gatilhos fiscais anunciados em agosto, com potencial de gerar uma economia de cerca de R$ 20 bilhões em 2027, foram bem recebidos pelo mercado. Na avaliação do senhor, o reajuste do Bolsa Família não enfraquece essa sinalização fiscal? Bruno Moretti: Remanejando despesas que vão ter projeção reduzida, porque os números estão mostrando isso, tem base técnica para isso, e transferindo para o Bolsa Família, é uma coisa entre despesas obrigatórias. Eu não altero essa lógica, eu não mudo minhas metas, eu não altero o volume de despesas obrigatórias dentro do orçamento, porque em boa medida o remanejamento virá de rubricas obrigatórias. Nós estamos tranquilos que não estamos alterando essa lógica que estamos implementando com uma série de medidas, em particular com os gatilhos, que você citou. E, repito, nós só podemos fazer isso porque fomos cautelosos.

g1: A quinze dias do primeiro turno das eleições, a medida não foi eleitoreira? Bruno Moretti: Se tivesse uma medida de caráter eleitoreiro, populista, o que aconteceria é que ela seria tomada no improviso. E, na verdade, nós só autorizamos, só demos o ateste orçamentário, que é função deste ministério, a partir do momento em que verificamos que havia o espaço fiscal.

g1: Esse diagnóstico não poderia ter sido captado antes? Bruno Moretti: Relatório tem prazos, é justamente um relatório bimestral. No último relatório, em julho, naquele momento a gente tinha R$ 17 bilhões bloqueados, então não havia espaço. Neste relatório, como eu estou dizendo, a gente vislumbrou o espaço para o desbloqueio. Parcela desse espaço será consumida pelo Bolsa Família. A gente tem uma área aqui que monitora de perto a dinâmica dessas despesas. Quando você percebe como se dá essa dinâmica, as informações vão sendo consolidadas na semana anterior à do relatório, que é esta semana, e não por acaso a decisão foi tomada esta semana. A proximidade com o cenário eleitoral foi casuística. Na verdade, o que importou aqui foi o recebimento das informações finais do relatório, nos dando a segurança de que havia o espaço fiscal.

g1: Por que a fila do INSS cai e a despesa com a Previdência cai também? Isso está acontecendo por conta do aumento dos indeferimentos? Bruno Moretti: Com todo o investimento em gestão que se fez na Previdência, você consegue hoje fazer a concessão para quem realmente precisa do benefício, para quem realmente tem direito àquele benefício que está sendo pleiteado, de uma forma muito mais eficiente, muito mais rápida, focando naqueles que têm direito. O que acontece aqui não é que a despesa previdenciária caia, é que a projeção de crescimento diminuiu. Ou seja, cresceu a um ritmo menor do que aquele que se previa, e esse crescimento a um ritmo menor tem a ver com a eficiência do processo de análise e concessão de benefícios feitos pela Previdência.

g1: Mas, ministro, o número de indeferimentos tem aumentado. Bruno Moretti: O indeferimento está dentro de uma média histórica do que era esperado, inclusive nos parâmetros que a gente tinha para absorver o crescimento dessa despesa no relatório, quando a gente fez lá atrás e fez o bloqueio para dar conta dessa despesa maior da Previdência.

g1: No mês passado, publicamos uma reportagem que mostra que a taxa de indeferimento alcançou quase 1 milhão de pedidos em junho. Bruno Moretti: Você precisa também entender que o histórico dos últimos anos não foi o melhor em termos de gestão dos benefícios. A mesma coisa do Bolsa Família, como eu disse. Quando você pega só os anos de 2021 e 2022, entende? É importante você olhar para uma média histórica mais ampla. Quando você olha, não é esse o cenário. O que está explicando não é um indeferimento maior do que a média histórica. Muito pelo contrário, hoje eu te diria que você tem as concessões [em ritmo maior].

g1: Em um eventual Lula 4, quais medidas de ajuste fiscal poderiam ser aplicadas? Bruno Moretti: Veja, aqui não é bem 'a' medida. A gente tem a responsabilidade, como governo, de encaminhar para o Congresso Nacional projetos de diretrizes orçamentárias e de orçamento, com essa trajetória de resultado primário capaz de colocar a dívida numa rota de sustentabilidade. E, do ponto de vista do orçamento, está, e no ano que vem, quais são as receitas, quanto você vai entregar desse esforço fiscal, projetando um esforço de 0,5% do PIB. O primeiro passo muito importante foi a vedação de se fazer novas renúncias no ano que vem. Do ponto de vista da despesa, também é preciso lembrar que temos vários instrumentos operando para além dos gatilhos. A própria revisão dos cadastros dos programas sociais segue em curso. É um trabalho permanente que, inclusive, viabilizou em parte essa projeção de um crescimento menos acentuado das despesas neste ano. Nós temos medidas de limitação de despesas que implementamos, contando com a parceria do Congresso. Por exemplo, Proagro e Seguro-Defesa. Essas despesas variavam muito ao longo do exercício. Se nós precisarmos de novas medidas, nós vamos tomar, porque vamos cumprir a trajetória fiscal com a qual estamos nos comprometendo para o ano que vem e ao longo dos próximos anos.

articles.title: Michael Saylor's Strategy jumps as the company says it bought more bitcoin
articles.summary: Strategy stock popped after the bitcoin holding company disclosed it bought more of the token and repurchased preferred stock last week.
articles.body:
What happened: Strategy ( MSTR ) stock rose more than 8% in premarket trading on Monday after the bitcoin holding company disclosed it bought more of the token and repurchased preferred stock last week.

The move pushed Strategy stock back into positive territory for the year — up about 1% since January — underscoring a major reversal after a number of tough months for the bitcoin holding giant.

What's behind the move: Strategy bought 950 bitcoin and repurchased about 1.77 million of its preferred stock ( STRC ) last week, it said in a Monday 8-K filing .

The bitcoin juggernaut also used another $57.4 million to fund dividends on preferred stock and outstanding interest payments. After those purchases, Strategy said its USD and cash reserves were $1.05 billion and $5.04 billion, respectively.

The disclosure came as other crypto stocks rallied , and bitcoin's price jumped more than 6% to trade above $85,000, its highest level since January. It followed a cryptic yet suggestive Sunday post on X from founder Michael Saylor, which read "a little more orange."

What else you need to know: Pressure on Strategy began mounting earlier this year as bitcoin and the wider crypto market descended into a prolonged winter.

The company's financial engineering began to sputter amid lower crypto prices as it was forced to sell bitcoin and stock to raise funds to meet debt and preferred stock dividend payments.

After an initial tumble following the failure of the crypto industry's big bill to advance in the Senate, Saylor, along with Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong , called for the industry to quickly look past the black eye, arguing the crypto world might be better off without the legislation.

articles.title: Investors must not forget their mission as AI hate grows
articles.summary: Investors have one job: Invest capital and, hopefully, earn a return.
articles.body:
Investors have one job: Invest capital and, hopefully, earn a return.

One can sit in their chair and fret over the AI extinction predictions floating around the internet, or they can keep their head down and make money off the technology (as they have probably done for over three years now).

"My job is to make money for clients," EMJ Capital founder Eric Jackson said on Yahoo Finance's Sozzi Unleashed when asked if the AI extinction fears have impacted his investing approach.

The backlash against artificial intelligence has intensified this month, and it goes far beyond people hating on data centers being built in their backyards.

Security has taken center stage after the high-profile Hugging Face incident . It has led various figures in tech to sound the alarm about the impact of AI, with some even questioning whether the human race will survive.

"Over the last few months, I have become convinced that fully addressing the risks requires even more prudence — not just investing in risk prevention, but pacing the rate of capabilities advancement so that risk prevention has time to keep up," Anthropic ( ANTH ) CEO Dario Amodei stated in a 3,800-word essay on Sept. 12. "We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of A.I. models. Progress will still seem fast, and we must make wise use of the time we gain."

OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) CEO Sam Altman said that he agreed with his rival, and then followed that up with a dark X post of his own.

Speaking at the annual Dreamforce software festival last week, Salesforce ( CRM ) co-founder and CEO Marc Benioff gave his bottom-line read on the debate over artificial intelligence: Leaders in AI have to step up and meet the safety moment.

"I know that we're all deeply disappointed with how the social media companies have operated over the last decade or more," Benioff told Yahoo Finance . "We know how many kids have been hurt. We've seen what has happened even to certain countries because of narratives on social media. And we cannot let AI be social media 2.0."

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the ' Power Players With Brian Sozzi' podcast and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team. Follow Sozzi on X @BrianSozzi , Instagram , and LinkedIn . Tips on stories? Email brian.sozzi@yahoofinance.com.

articles.title: Suze Orman Warns This Common 401(k) Mistake Could Cost You Thousands
articles.summary: Suze Orman calls the Roth 401(k) a must-have for anyone serious about building tax-free wealth for retirement.
articles.body:
If you're taking a set-it-and-forget-it approach to your retirement accounts, you could be missing out on one of the most powerful strategies available.

Money expert and all-around financial guru Suze Orman calls the Roth 401(k) a must-have for anyone serious about building tax-free wealth for retirement. Unlike a traditional 401(k), a Roth 401(k) allows you to pay taxes now and enjoy tax-free withdrawals later, which could potentially save you thousands in retirement.

Here's why Orman says making this switch could be one of the smartest money moves you'll ever make.

Most Americans Skip This Valuable 401(k) Option

"If you have a retirement plan through work, chances are your employer offers a great option," Orman shared on LinkedIn . "Yet, for reasons I can't understand, you aren't signing up for this great option. I am talking about being able to save for retirement with a Roth 401(k)."

According to Vanguard data, 86% of 401(k) plans offer participants the option to save in a Roth 401(k).

"That is fantastic," she said. "But here's the part that has me pulling my hair out: Vanguard also reported that fewer than 1 in 5 participants who had this option chose to save in a Roth 401(k). That is nuts."

Orman said that if you can opt into a Roth 401(k) for the coming year, you should do it -- it's easier than you might think.

"I am not talking about moving all the savings you already have in your 401(k)," she said. "All that you should change is where your new 2026 contributions go."

Traditional vs. Roth 401(k): What You Need To Know

The key difference between a traditional and Roth 401(k) is when you pay tax.

"With a traditional 401(k), the amount you contribute each year reduces your taxable income," Orman said. "For example, if you earn $85,000 and contribute $10,000 to a traditional 401(k), your taxable income from those earnings is reported as $75,000."

However, 100% of withdrawals from a traditional 401(k) are taxed as ordinary income. A Roth 401(k) has a different tax setup.

"You get no upfront tax break on the money you contribute to the account. But once you are retired, 100% of your withdrawals will be tax-free," Orman said. "And there is no [required minimum distribution] with a Roth 401(k). You don't have to make withdrawals at any point if you don't need the money."

Why Suze Orman Recommended Roth 401(k) Contributions

Orman believes that utilizing a mix of traditional and Roth 401(k) plans will set you up for financial success in retirement.

"For those of you who have spent years saving in a traditional 401(k), it would be so smart to now focus on building up savings in a Roth 401(k)," she said. "Having money you will not owe any tax on in retirement is going to be a great advantage.

articles.title: Kairos Power gets up to $100M from Samsung group to build nuclear reactor for Google
articles.summary: Future Google supplier Kairos Power inked a deal with Samsung C&T to help build its first 50-megawatt nuclear power plant.
articles.body:
Kairos Power has picked engineering firm Samsung C&T to help build its 50-megawatt demonstration reactor for Google , which the nuclear startup is aiming to have completed by 2030.

As part of the deal, Samsung C&T will make an equity investment in Kairos and provide "in-kind" engineering services, the combination of which is worth up to $100 million, Kairos Power said Monday. The equity investment will make up $70 million of the total, a Kairos spokesperson told TechCrunch.

Samsung C&T has built or helped build about a dozen nuclear reactors around the globe.

Kairos is part of a wave of nuclear startups that have benefited from the surge in power demand from AI data centers. Google first signed a deal with the company in fall 2024 , calling on Kairos to build nuclear reactors capable of generating about half a gigawatt of electricity by 2035.

Currently, Kairos is building two reactors in Oak Ridge, Tennessee. The first, Hermes 1, is a low-power demonstrator that will help the company refine its commercial design. The second, Hermes 2, is Kairos' first commercial-scale reactor. Output from Hermes will count as the first 50 megawatts of its deal with Google.

The startup received approval from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission in late 2024 to build the reactors. It expects Hermes 2 to begin operating in 2030, in line with its original agreement with Google.

Hermes 2 will be a fluoride salt-cooled high-temperature reactor, a design that has been floated for years but never built at commercial scale. Fluoride salts have high boiling points, which will help keep pressure levels low. That, in turn, will limit the risk of high-pressure blowouts in case of any parts failures.

Kairos is also using a relatively new form of nuclear fuel known as TRISO, which encapsulates tiny seeds of uranium fuel in layers of ceramic and carbon, which are then loaded into billiard ball-sized spheres. The arrangement is intended to prevent meltdowns.

The startup has about five years to get its first power plant up and running, which is an accelerated but manageable timeline in the nuclear industry. To fulfill the terms of its deal with Google, Kairos will need to move even faster on subsequent reactors, something Samsung C&T might be able to help with.

articles.title: Maye Musk: Elon really wants to live on Mars in the coming decades
articles.summary: A rare glimpse into Elon Musk from his mother, Maye.
articles.body:
Listen and subscribe to Power Players with Brian Sozzi on Apple Podcasts , Amazon Music , Spotify , YouTube , or wherever you find your favorite podcasts.

Elon Musk's next few decades may look as eventful as his past few decades building Tesla ( TSLA ), SpaceX ( SPCX ), X, the Boring Company, Neuralink, and PayPal ( PYPL ).

Or so says his supermodel mom, Maye Musk.

"I think he really would like to live in the city of Mars," Maye Musk said on the Power Players with Brian Sozzi podcast (see video above or listen below). "That's what he's saying. But, you know, I can't say what's going on in his mind because he comes up with these amazing thoughts. When he said to me, 'I'm going to send satellites into space,' and I said why, … he said, 'If you're stuck in the middle of an ocean or in the middle of a forest or on top of a hill and you are injured and you can't contact anyone, then you will die.' So he wants to prevent this."

In her new memoir, "Timeless: The Art of Reinvention and Resilience at Any Age," Musk offers a candid look into the personal hardships and career pivots from dietitian to world-renowned model that have shaped her life's journey.

The book details her experiences navigating financial instability in the wake of fleeing from an abusive marriage to Errol Musk, raising ambitious children in Elon, Kimball , and Tosca, and continually redefining her brand late in life.

Musk began her modeling career at age 15 in South Africa, balancing print campaigns with her studies to earn two master's degrees in dietetics and nutritional science. After leaving Errol Musk, she raised her three children as a working single mother while building a private nutrition practice.

Rather than fading with age, Musk's modeling career exploded into global prominence after she turned 60 when she embraced her natural silver hair.

She went on to shatter industry age barriers by becoming a CoverGirl ambassador at age 69 and gracing the cover of the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit issue at 74.

Musk contended that the public often doesn't understand Elon — a natural response from a mom, of course. She frequently takes to X to defend him.

"If you did have one [a kid] and somebody's insulting them when they're doing good, you would come down on them like crazy," Musk said. "I try to be as nice as I can, but you don't insult my kids."

articles.title: Meta stock soars 11% on price target increase, Muse AI downloads
articles.summary: Meta rocketed higher Monday, closing out the trading day up more than 11%.
articles.body:
Meta ( META ) stock rocketed more than 11% Monday, after Wells Fargo raised its price target on the company and its Meta Muse AI agent app hit the top spot on Apple's ( AAPL ) App Store.

In a note to investors, Ken Gawrelski raised his price target on the company from $640 to $796.

Gawrelski pointed to Meta's recent successful AI model launches, including its latest Muse Spark offering and the Muse assistant, as proof that the company "now has a story to tell" with regard to its AI capabilities and services.

Meta's AI fortunes mark a sharp turnaround from last year, when the company was dealing with AI model delays and questions about the billions it is spending on its AI infrastructure build-out.

Since then, CEO Mark Zuckerberg has rebuilt Meta's AI lab, hiring Scale.AI co-founder and CEO Alexandr Wang as Meta's chief AI officer.

The company now offers several models within its Muse AI family.

The price target change and strong showing from Muse come ahead of Meta's upcoming Meta Connect conference on Wednesday.

Zuckerberg is scheduled to deliver a keynote outlining the company's upcoming plans across both its AI and wearables devices.

Meta stock has struggled over the past 12 months, falling roughly 5% versus Amazon ( AMZN ) stock, which is up 38%, and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) stock, which rose 11%. Microsoft ( MSFT ) has barely outpaced Meta, which is down 4%.

But Meta stock has jumped significantly over the past three months, soaring 30%. Only Microsoft outpaced Meta, rocketing 35%.

articles.title: Tech stocks power market surge as bond yields and oil prices tumble
articles.summary: Tech stocks surged Monday, with the Nasdaq 100 recording its single best day since early August as a wave of euphoria swept over the markets.
articles.body: Tech stocks surged Monday, with the Nasdaq 100 recording its single best day since early August as a wave of euphoria swept over the markets. The broader Nasdaq Composite index also rose 2.2% to a new all-time closing high. The S&P 500 index soared by 1.5%, also its best day since early last month. The Dow rose more than 360 points, or 0.7%. Chip companies such as ARM Holdings, which spiked 17%, and Intel, which rose 12%, accounted for some of the Nasdaq’s best performing stocks. AMD shares rose nearly 10%, and the company hit a $1 trillion valuation for the first time. Meta Platforms rose a stunning 11.4%, adding nearly $200 billion in market value, fueled by optimism around its AI ambitions and its recently released Muse AI assistant. Monday ranked as Meta’s best one-day stock performance since the global market tariff turmoil of April 2025. The buying was not restricted to tech stocks, however. Shares of Moderna powered higher by 12%. The S&P industrial, real estate and consumer discretionary sectors also posted strong gains. After Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery reached a deal earlier Monday with state attorneys general that likely paves the way for them to close their merger, shares of each company jumped more than 10%. The market moves were largely attributable to a report over the weekend from Fox News Channel’s Trey Yingst, who said he had spoken to President Donald Trump. “The president said he would possibly be open to meeting with Iranian President Pezeshkian” during the United Nations General Assembly in New York this week, Yingst reported Sunday. The reporting raised hopes among investors that the monthslong freeze in any U.S.-Iran talks could end this week, potentially clearing the way for renewed oil traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Oil prices dropped sharply as a result, with Brent crude oil closing the session Monday at $100.34 per barrel, down 3.4% for the day. U.S. crude oil slid to $95.78, down 4.5% for the session. Also pushing oil prices lower were reports of an increase in Saudi Arabia’s oil flows from Bloomberg News, which cited satellite imagery of oil supertankers filling up. Earlier in the day, Brent dipped below $100 per barrel for the first time since Sept. 9. The S&P’s energy sector was the index’s biggest laggard on Monday, declining 2.5% as the prospect of higher profits evaporated. Monday’s drops marked oil’s fourth straight day of declines, bringing its total decline to 9.5% since Wednesday. Oil prices remain sharply elevated this year, despite its drop in recent days. Since the start of the year, oil has risen more than 65%. As oil prices fell, bond yields followed, fueled by hopes that cheaper oil could lead to lower gas prices, and an overall easing of the inflationary forces rippling through the U.S. economy. In their second straight day of declines, the 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.96%, after trading as high as 5.02% last week. That specific Treasury bond heavily influences consumer borrowing rates. Still, the average 30-year fixed rate mortgage was still 7.19% on Monday, according to Mortgage News Daily. On Sunday night, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and U.S. Trade Rep. Jamieson Greer hailed “very successful” trade discussions with their counterparts from China. The delegations also discussed AI and potentially lower tariffs on a swath of goods. The prospect of positive developments on the U.S.-China trade front also provided some hope to investors, but not that much. On Monday, Greer shot down speculation about a possible extension of the U.S.-China trade deal that set to expire in November. “Our sense is we aren’t going to have the extension today,” he told Bloomberg News.

articles.title: New Zealand trade pact to take effect on Oct 20, to give duty-free access
articles.summary: India Business News: NEW DELHI: The India-New Zealand free trade agreement (FTA) will come into force on Oct 20 (Dusshera), providing duty-free access to 100% of India’s e.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The India-New Zealand free trade agreement (FTA) will come into force on Oct 20 (Dusshera), providing duty-free access to 100% of India’s exports, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal announced Monday. And, talks with Canada for a comprehensive economic partnership agreement (CEPA) are moving in top gear.“The next 90 days should be a very defining period in the Canada-India relationship. Both sides have resolved to fast-track negotiations, in view of which our team is now slated to go for the fifth round on Oct 5,” Goyal told reporters. The fourth round of negotiations concluded on Sept 18 and the next one is scheduled in just around a fortnight, indicating that two sides are keen to clinch a deal soon. Canada is in the midst of a trade battle with the US and is seen to be keen to expand its trade footprint and reduce its reliance on its neighbour.India’s major exports to Canada include pharmaceuticals, iron and steel, seafood, cotton garments, electronic goods and chemicals. Key imports from Canada include pulses, pearls and semi-precious stones, coal, fertilisers, paper and crude petroleum. Trade between the two countries stood at $30.4 billion in 2025, with an aim to double it to $70 billion by 2030. Besides, Goyal also expressed confidence regarding the trade pact with Chile. “In the coming few months, we will hear some good news,” he said.Regarding the trade agreement with New Zealand, Goyal said it will help boost bilateral trade between the two countries to Rs 35,000 crore and will help facilitate $20 billion investments in India over next 15 years in sectors such as startups, manufacturing and infrastructure.“We are taking forward the next important milestone in our bilateral economic partnership, reflecting our shared commitment to build a stronger and a more ambitious economic partnership,” Goyal said. The two countries had inked the pact in April this year.Currently, New Zealand maintains tariffs of up to 10% on key Indian goods, including ceramics, carpets, automobiles, textiles and auto components. Goyal added that the pact also establishes an agricultural productivity partnership whereby New Zealand’s technology will meet India’s scale and growing demand.For New Zealand, the pact will provide preferential access to the largest and fastest growing economy of the world, he said.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. articles.title: Interests of charitable trust may differ from that of co: JP Morgan chairman & CEO Jamie Dimon
articles.summary: India Business News: MUMBAI: JP Morgan is the world’s most valuable bank, and its chairman and CEO Jamie Dimon is the longest serving chief of a large global bank. In an i.
articles.body: MUMBAI: JP Morgan is the world’s most valuable bank, and its chairman and CEO Jamie Dimon is the longest serving chief of a large global bank. In an interview with TOI, Dimon speaks of what it takes to run America’s largest bank and his definition of success.You completed two decades at JPMorgan this year. What does it take to run a bank successfully for two decades? Is it a conservative approach?I took over Bank One in 2000 which effectively took control of JP Morgan, so it has been closer to 26 years. I consider myself conservative, but banking always involves risk. Good risk-taking is analytical, not guesswork: assess competitors, costs, capital, liquidity and stress scenarios.You need to know the details, study the data and be honest about results. Success is not just profit; it’s about customers, products, execution and how you compare with the best. Have curiosity, courage and grit, and tell the board more about what went wrong than what went right. That is how you improve.When you’re already the most valuable, largest bank, how do you measure success as a CEO?Ultimately, value matters, but a good company is more than profit. Are you retaining, hiring and training good people and building a culture of openness, curiosity and ambition across technology, products and systems? Maximising profit means little if products, systems or compliance fail and regulators are unhappy. You have to judge the whole business.We’re seeing a lot of leadership changes in India. What should the objectives be for a CEO? Should it be just shareholder returns and customer satisfaction, or should it go beyond that?It is about the whole institution: products, services, systems, people, culture, ethics and compliance. In India, that means serving clients while meeting govt and regulatory expectations. If a new system strengthens the business for 20 years, build it even if it hurts near-term profits or the share price. We also measure market share, competition and customer satisfaction because all three matter.You introduced initiatives to help redevelop Detroit. Do you think that large institutions like JPMorgan should go beyond their role in just banking and look at benefiting society? And what’s the best structure for doing good?Absolutely. It is part of our job. In India, we look to help lift the country through how we operate, serve our clients and raise capital. Since 2019, we’ve raised and provided clients with more than $84 billion in capital and credit. And since 2015, we have contributed more than $90 million in donations and helped more than 100,000 young people develop skills and access careers through our partnerships with nonprofits.A healthy company helps clients and lifts society, and philanthropy must also deliver results. In Detroit, we made a multiyear commitment covering jobs, skills and healthcare, bringing all our businesses together. We learned from it and now apply the model in other cities. For CEOs, lifting society means doing both the commercial and philanthropic work.In Detroit, we had a great leader in the mayor who said, “I’ll work with anybody who helps me.” He didn’t say, “I’m not going to speak to business. I’m not going to speak to philanthropy. I’m not going to speak to civil society.” He got everyone to the table to address basic needs such as housing, street lights, ambulances, policing, taxes and schools. He asked for help, acted on it and changed the city.A lot of business houses in Europe and in India, like the Tatas, have a structure where they are owned by charitable trusts, and that’s the route used to do good. Do you think that is the right structure for doing good?I’m not saying it’s always bad. A company should be run properly, and the interests of a charitable trust could be very different from the interests of a company. A company has got to be healthy and vibrant and have proper governance. A structure like that sometimes works against that.I have seen boards in big American companies that are more obsessed with how they look than whether the company is building great products. And that is bad not just for the company, but for society. If the company isn’t healthy and vibrant, if it has the wrong goals, then it’s bad for jobs, capital formation and the country. So you’ve got to be quite careful with something like that.I understand what you are referring to, and, to be clear, I think the world of Chandra. He’s done an extraordinary job in creating value for the foundations. Corporate governance is critical for a successful economy and its companies, and if changes are needed to corporate structures, they should be made.When I walk into the boardroom, I ask the questions: “What’s the right thing to do for the company, its clients and the community?”When do you think the Fed rate hike will start hurting and put stress on businesses?At this point, it doesn’t, but at some point it will start to put stress. I don’t think the short rate is that important; I think it’s more about the 10-year rate. I don’t think one more 25-basis-point rate hike would do it. I’m very sympathetic to those facing stress, but I don’t put that in the systemic category.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: GST rate rejig helps consumers upgrade
articles.summary: India Business News: NEW DELHI/MUMBAI: A year after GST rates were cut, automobile dispatches have continued to climb. Several two-wheeler users moved to four-wheelers as .
articles.body: NEW DELHI/MUMBAI: A year after GST rates were cut, automobile dispatches have continued to climb. Several two-wheeler users moved to four-wheelers as price cuts improved affordability, TV buyers have shifted towards larger sets and consumer goods volumes picked up in the Oct-Dec quarter, although they are now under pressure due to the West Asia crisis.Passenger vehicle dispatches reached a record 12.7 lakh units in April–June 2026, up 25.9% from a year earlier, according to Siam. Two-wheeler dispatches rose 20.3% to 56.3 lakh units. Siam has cited lower GST rates and easier financing among the factors supporting demand. Its figures measure supplies to dealers, rather than purchases by customers.Television shipments tell a different story. India’s smart TV shipments grew 10% year-on-year in Oct–Dec 2025, according to Counterpoint Research, before falling 3% in Jan-March 2026. TVs sized 55 inches and above were the fastest-growing category in the March quarter, accounting for nearly one-third of shipments.The trend, however, got stalled because of the uncertainty triggered by Operation Epic Fury US and Israel launched against Iran on Feb 28 and Counterpoint’s TV tracker recorded a 9.8% decline in shipments in April–June. GST on TVs above 32 inches, including 55-inch models, was slashed from 28% to 18% last Sept.Keshav Bansal, director at Intex Technologies, said the cut created “a meaningful affordability window” for bigger TVs. Intex’s consumer durables business grew 80% in FY26, with smart TVs among the drivers, he said. But “unit volumes have not risen in proportion to value growth; the more significant shift has been in product mix,” as buyers chose larger screens and better technology.Bansal said lower GST also supported air-conditioner demand, alongside a favourable summer and a lower comparison base. Rising input costs, including memory chips for TVs, and the cost of meeting newer energy-efficiency norms for ACs have since absorbed part of the tax benefit, he said.“In the long-term, it is definitely a positive, especially with people looking to move to branded products. But there is some impact in the short run due to the recent increase in input prices. Also, full refund of input tax credit will help in offsetting some of the cost,” said Liberty Shoes executive director Anupam Bansal.FMCG companies initially saw an improvement in demand after the rate changes. Volume growth picked up at companies, including Hindustan Unilever, Marico and Dabur. Nestlé India reported its strongest volume growth in five years in the Dec 2025 quarter, attributing it partly to a market recovery supported by GST benefits.That early lift has come under pressure as companies raised prices to offset higher costs. Companies and analysts are keeping a close watch on sales in the current quarter.Get the latest Business News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: India Business News: NEW DELHI: Core sector grew 4.8% in Aug, compared with 6.2% a year ago, official data released on Monday showed. Sequentially, the growth marked a slo.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Core sector grew 4.8% in Aug, compared with 6.2% a year ago, official data released on Monday showed. Sequentially, the growth marked a slowdown from a downwardly revised figure of 5% in July and was at three-month low.Output in the energy dominant industries like natural gas (-4.9%), coal (-3.8%) and crude oil (-3.6%), barring the refinery products (2.6%), saw sequential contraction, reflecting the impact of the prolonged conflict in West Asia.On the other hand, output in the infrastructure dominant industries like steel (3.4%), cement (12.5%) and electricity (11.6%) showed positive growth in Aug.Output in the newly added iron ore industry decelerated (5.5%) during the month, while fertiliser output (-12.4%) contracted for the sixth consecutive month.Bank of Baroda chief economist Madan Sabnavis said higher growth in refinery products is due to exports and domestic consumption, while fertiliser production is down as sowing season slows and imports increase.The eight core sectors constitute 40.3% of the Index of Industrial Production (IIP), which measures output in the country's industrial sector, and is considered a bellwether for the latter's performance.Get the latest Business News and Live updates.
